items.title: 朝鮮發佈金正恩照片：為何他的死亡傳言總是捲土重來？
items.description: 在未經證實的傳言傳開後，朝鮮官媒發布了這位獨裁者與其女兒的照片。
items.content:
朝鮮發佈金正恩照片：為何他的死亡傳言總是捲土重來？
  - Author, 碧嘉蘭（Laura Bicker）
  - Role, BBC駐中國記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
金正恩看起來對於一名據傳因腦出血去世的人而言，健康狀況出奇地良好。
朝鮮（北韓）官方報章《勞動新聞》刊登的照片顯示，這名42歲獨裁者正與女兒參觀一個據報為服裝及鞋履展覽的活動。
這些照片發布前數小時，一名居於美國的中國異見人士在毫無證據支持下聲稱，金正恩已被送往北京一間醫院，陷入昏迷，並已死亡。
對於密切關注朝鮮的人來說，這類傳言幾乎已成為例行公事。
在這個全球最封閉的國家之一，事實往往難以核實，為各種猜測提供了沃土。
這次最新說法來自謝萬軍。他自稱是中國民主黨主席，該組織遭中國當局禁止。過去他曾散播未經證實的說法，包括有關中國領導人習近平去世的猜測。
謝萬軍聲稱，金正恩因嚴重腦出血被送往北京，原因是朝鮮缺乏相關醫療設施為其治療。
他稱金正恩其後死亡，遺體被秘密運回朝鮮，而政權一直隱瞞其死訊。
然而，這些照片呈現出截然不同的情況。
照片中的金正恩正在查看展品，身旁是金主愛及其慣常隨行的一眾官員。
雖然無法確定這些照片究竟拍攝於何時，但還有其他理由令人懷疑這項說法。
如果金正恩健康狀況突然惡化，朝鮮境外很可能會出現一些跡象。
中國可能會加強邊境保安，以應對潛在不穩定局勢或難民潮。朝鮮駐外使館周邊活動也可能增加。在韓國（南韓）的脫北者，經常透過中國邊境一帶的非正式網絡獲取資訊。但上述情況都未有發生。
與此同時，韓聯社引述韓國情報官員表示，他們沒有聽到任何足以支持相關報導的消息。
這次傳言也令人聯想到過去多次錯誤警報。
2020年，一名知名脫北者聲稱，在接受心血管手術後，自己「99%確定」金正恩已經死亡。不久之後，金正恩公開露面，相關說法不攻自破。
那麼，為何這類傳言總是一再出現？
第一個原因是接班問題。
朝鮮已由金氏家族統治三代，但金正恩之後會發生什麼事，遠比其前任時期更不明朗。
金日成花了數十年時間為兒子金正日接班作準備。到金日成於1994年去世時，接班安排已經牢固建立。金正日的權力交接相對順利。
金正恩的崛起則更迅速，也更加充滿風險。
2008年金正日中風後，他的幼子迅速獲得提拔。到父親於2011年去世時，他已被公開確認為未來領袖。
即使如此，金正恩仍花了數年時間鞏固權力，清洗對手並剷除他認為構成威脅的人物。
如今，韓國情報機構相信，他可能正將女兒培養為接班人。她近年愈來愈頻繁出現在重要活動及軍事展示場合。
但外界認為她年僅13歲。朝鮮從未由女性領導，而她也未被正式指定為繼承人。她年紀尚輕，在任何權力鬥爭中都可能處於弱勢。
所有這些不確定因素，都有助解釋為何有關金正恩健康狀況的傳言總能引起巨大關注。
第二個原因是，這些傳言並非全然沒有可能。
金正恩過重且吸煙量大。韓國國家情報院曾多次警告，其生活方式令他罹患心血管疾病的風險較高。而心臟疾病及中風在金氏家族中亦有家族病史。
如果金正恩真的發生任何意外，對周邊國家及更廣泛的國際社會而言，後果都十分重大。任何突如其來的領導層危機，都會帶來有關朝鮮核武控制權以及政治不穩定風險的艱難問題。
權力鬥爭是否會令強硬派採取更具攻擊性的行動？社會動盪是否可能在中朝邊境引發難民危機？
這些問題不僅令北京和首爾憂慮，也令在韓國駐有約2.8萬名士兵的華盛頓關注。
情報機構密切監察金正恩，以便為任何消息做好準備。
由於朝鮮依然是一個資訊黑洞，它也很容易成為虛假報導的目標。
只有極少數人能夠定期接觸其最高領導人。即使是情報機構，也難以獲得可靠資訊，而流出的消息大多都附有大量保留條件，被描述為「未經證實」或「極有可能」，而非已獲確認的事實。
外界亦懷疑，朝鮮政權刻意製造混亂，釋放誤導性資訊，以掩蓋國內真實情況。
因此，當那些專門負責掌握相關情況的人都未能取得這類重要消息時，很難相信謝萬軍竟能偶然獲得如此重大資訊。
他可能只是想吸引注意。
又或者，他可能希望藉著突顯北京與平壤的關係而令北京難堪，儘管這種關係早已是世人皆知的事實。
無論其動機為何，謝萬軍遠非第一個利用朝鮮領導層不確定性的人。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
items.description: 在普京建議三方於APEC期間進行會談後，特朗普表示願意參與，強調會談重點將是無核化問題。目前中方尚未就三方會談表態。
items.content:
普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
美國總統特朗普下月將赴中國，出席11月18日至19日在深圳舉行的亞太經合組織（APEC）峰會。俄羅斯總統普京早前提出，在峰會期間舉行中美俄三方元首會晤，外界關注這場會談成事的機率及可能涉及的議題。
10月19日，特朗普給出回應。他表示願意參與會晤，但強調重點將是無核化問題，而非結束俄烏戰爭。這與普京的初始意向——商討烏克蘭問題——並不一致。
中國外交部發言人毛寧目前僅表示「沒有可以提供的信息」，未明確表態。烏克蘭外交部長西比加（Andrii Sybiha）則在社交平台X發文批評，稱舉行此類會晤只會助長普京的「自我膨脹」，「讓他獲得不必要的地位」，鼓勵其繼續發動戰爭。
三國元首此前從未舉行過正式的三方會談，而這場計劃中的會面也不會有烏克蘭總統澤連斯基參與。若最終敲定，將成為國際外交史上的重大事件。
「雅爾塔會議2.0」？
「三方會談」的想法由普京提出。《華爾街日報》援引前俄羅斯情報官員透露，普京在10月9日與特朗普的通話中，提議與美中元首就烏克蘭問題舉行會晤。
該次通話同時促成雙方協議，美國將從俄羅斯進口柴油以降低油價。
報道指出，普京正試圖利用與特朗普日益密切的關係解決俄烏問題。前俄羅斯情報官員又向該報表示，普京希望這次三方會談能成為劃分全球勢力範圍的「第二次雅爾塔會議」。
雅爾塔會議是二戰末期美國、英國、蘇聯領導人在克里米亞的雅爾塔舉行的首腦峰會。當時，三個大國領導人制定了二戰後的世界新秩序以及利益分配，形成了所謂的「雅爾塔體系」，深刻影響到了此後的世界格局。
特朗普的考量與烏克蘭的壓力
近幾個星期以來，特朗普與澤連斯基的關係急劇惡化。特朗普向記者表示：「（澤連斯基）早就應該解決這場戰爭。如果他當初聽我的話，早就能達成一份好得多的協議。」
面對中期選舉迫近與油價高企，特朗普將責任轉嫁至澤連斯基攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠的行為，指責對方「不想結束這場戰爭」。
不過能源專家普遍認為，伊朗戰爭才是柴油價格上漲的主要原因，而俄羅斯承諾出售的燃料量也難以影響市場供應。
前美國國防部政策分析師、美國南加州大學中歐研究中心主任羅伯特·英格利希（Robert English）向BBC分析道：「美烏領導人的關係已跌至前所未有的低點。」
他指出，特朗普擔心國會中期選舉落敗，「因此他再次施壓，希望促成某種烏克蘭和平協議」。英格利希認為，特朗普轉向支持普京，是因為「他相信這是最快結束戰爭的方法」。
但英格利希說，這種施壓不一定有效：「當特朗普以這種方式批評澤連斯基，烏克蘭人反而會更加團結在他身邊。」他補充，歐洲盟友亦會在能力許可範圍內，向烏克蘭提供更多援助。
「（烏克蘭崩潰）或許是特朗普和普京所期望的，但現實並非如此。」英格利希說。
北京為何不回應？
目前中方對三方會談仍未公開表態。《華爾街日報》引述分析指，在中國舉行此類峰會，將是習近平提升中國外交斡旋地位的重要一步。華盛頓智庫史汀生中心中國項目主任孫韻表示，中國希望被視為大國之間的樞紐，並可能成為美國和俄羅斯之間的調解人。
不過即使會談促成，三方討論的也未必集中在核武問題。上週（16日），外交部發言人毛寧曾表示，中國核力量與美俄完全不在同一量級，現階段要求中方參與核裁軍談判「不公平、不合理，亦不可行」。
報道又引述知情人士稱，有中國官員擔心會談涉及的地緣政治問題，會掩蓋中方利用APEC展示區域角色的計劃。
與此同時，北京正試圖在支持普京與維繫中歐經濟聯繫之間取得平衡，三方會晤或會使中國直接捲入烏克蘭衝突，觸發歐洲各國強烈反對。

items.title: 香港演員鍾雪瑩、袁澧林發聲之後，她們親述被性別冒犯的經歷
items.description: BBC中文訪問了四位來自不同行業的女性，了解言語冒犯是如何在工作環境中出現；當性別冒犯被包裝成「玩笑」，她們是如何應對。
items.content:
香港演員鍾雪瑩、袁澧林發聲之後，她們親述被性別冒犯的經歷
  - Author, 余美霞
  - Role, BBC中文記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 8 分鐘
兩位香港知名「90後」女演員近日在網絡社交媒體上，揭露一名本地文藝娛樂記者對她們使用性相關冒犯言論，引發社會迴響。
10月13日，金馬影后鍾雪瑩先發表限時動態，對該記者以「激罕色慾演出」來描述她在新電影中的演出表達反感。袁澧林（Angela Yuen）跟帖聲援，發布一則近3000字文章，表示約半年前受訪時，同被對方形容像是「夜總會陪酒」。
袁澧林隨後再講述自己在行業中遭遇的性騷擾經歷。她形容，每一次「小玩笑」都在鞏固「女性被物化的體系」，指出冒犯者「可以是『任何行業』中的『任何人』」。
在香港演藝圈，願意公開談論性別冒犯的女性並不多見。二人的發聲觸發不少網民發帖，講述自己的經歷。BBC中文聆聽四位來自不同行業女性的經歷，了解這類言語冒犯是如何在工作環境中出現；當性別冒犯被包裝成「玩笑」，她們是如何應對。
【提示：以下內容涉及性相關言語騷擾與冒犯，敬請斟酌閱讀。】
「他們知道沒有後果」
鴿子（化名），90後，香港電影從業者
其實在Angela發聲之前，我和其他曾受言語騷擾的同事已經想發聲很久，但是一直沒有渠道。我們沒有名氣，你知道吧？槍打出頭鳥。發聲了，我們一定是大輸家。
言語騷擾，我每一天都會遇到。那可以是針對你的身材、外貌，也可以是他們在對話中刻意加入色情元素，目的就是想看到你嬌羞、不知所措，從中獲得支配的快感。
還記得剛剛入行，學院教授特意提醒我，要我再三「想清楚」。他說，「外面的人」不是那麼美好。但那時候，我還沒有感受到這一行業的惡意，反而對創作充滿衝勁。
到大三實習，我迎來了當頭棒喝。當時我在一家本地電視台擔任節目編導。這個由男性主導的行業，編輯從20到50歲都有。有一次我穿短褲上班，有人帶頭叫：「有腿看！」然後數個編輯一起湧過來。
他們覺得這樣好玩、在調戲我。我曾向較年輕的男編輯反映不適，卻獲回覆：「你穿短褲，就是對自己身材有自信、想給人看嘛。」我覺得很委屈——我在大學經常穿短褲，從未感受到淫邪的目光。為什麼來到這裡，就會變成是我的刻意展示呢？
到後來畢業正式入行，我才知道原來這樣的凝視和說笑是常態。原因就是因為冒犯者知道你不會反抗，也知道這樣做不會有後果。
言語性騷擾的發生就像呼吸一樣自然，講這些話的人大多都是在行裡打滾很久的前輩。
有人會以「身材好好那個」來稱呼我；有人每次看到我的腿都會點評「很長」。比如我跟一個前輩打招呼，他會笑着假裝要解開褲子，「拿東西」出來。
你知道有些長途司機當沒時間上廁所時，他們會用瓶子解決。有一次，我看到一名劇組司機前輩身旁有一瓶褐黃色的液體，就有點噁心地問他那是不是尿。他笑笑回我：「這瓶口太小了，（我的陽具）裝不下。」
我自問已經算是個性別意識很強的人，也不算怕事。但「愣住」往往是我第一反應。有時候，在場的人會幫忙打圓場，說為我「討公道」。所以無論當下有多生氣，我會覺得「發爛渣（發脾氣、撒潑）」是一件不厚道的事。
但有一次我真的忍不住。一次臨近下班，一名前輩在眾目睽睽下，把手搭在一位較膽小的女同事肩膀上，連續揑了好幾下。我馬上喝止他：「縮開你的X手！」在場的人都愣住。但那位前輩沒有退開，反而像報復一樣，整個人再挨近那同事。
當我再喝止時，他突然走到我面前，我和他之間只隔了一隻手掌的距離。當下其實我很害怕，不知道他會做什麼事，但我要故作鎮定。對望幾秒後，他氣憤地丟下一句：「整容樣！」然後就走開。
那位前輩在1980年代入行，很多同行都是他帶出來的，所以事情發生時，和我交情不錯的人也不敢出來「做架両（給我撐腰）」。
我有把事情跟上司反映。男部門主管說：「所以我不會給我女兒做這一行。」女高層則表示：「我當年更誇張啦！我有被製片問過要不要跟他回家、又被問有多久沒有跟男朋友做愛。」
演藝行業是一個缺人手的行業，沒有人想把事情鬧大。我覺得很沮喪、絕望。
但其實，我並不覺得這些男性無法理解女性的處境。他們也有跟過同志導演拍戲。在那情況下，這群男人就會自動代入「被害者」的角色——他們害怕自己被侵犯、被凝視。假如他們換位思考，就會知道女生每天都在面對這些不安。
況且他們也不是一視同仁。他們從不會這樣騷擾女高層，反而專挑一些隨和怕事的女生下手。說到底，他們就是欺善怕惡。所以我覺得很不公平。我作為女生，在職場上侊似要付出巨大努力來證明自己，才會機會得到尊重、不再被當作成調戲對象。
但這不就很荒謬嗎？
我很感謝 Angela 願意站出來講話，她的影響力最起碼可以在短時間裡，讓行業裡的人收斂一下。但長遠下去，至少在這行業，最有效的方法始終是由上而下去推動——當有話語權的人設下原則，並且認真和嚴格執行，冒犯才不會再被當作是一個「玩笑」。
「你不是記者嗎？自己怎麼不發聲呢？」
陳子凝（化名），80後，前香港新聞工作者
我覺得在這一行，最大的壓抑或委屈之一，就是我們經常說要為別人發聲、爭取公義。但諷刺的是，你會發現有些同事在幫別人發聲，但同時會開性別玩笑。這個反差特別大。
大學畢業後，我進了一家本地報章工作。有時我們要跟遊行示威現場採訪，天氣熱，我會穿背心短褲，這時我會被攝影師嘲諷着「很少布」。我成功做了一個獨家訪問，老闆會打趣說：「你訪到他是因為你漂亮」、「你那天是不是穿了短裙出去呀？」
你就會覺得，你好像要比其他人更加努力，才能確保成果不會被視為「性別紅利」。我甚至想過，是不是只要不打扮、隨便穿，大家就會看到我的能力？但我不甘心，因為問題並不在我身上。
受到這些對待的頻率，除了與性別有關，還取決於權力和階層。你的年資決定你的話語權，也影響你會被笑多久。
我當年是一張白紙入行，還很在意如何在行業立足發展、也在意別人的目光。這些不適的經歷會讓你覺得職場本來就是如此、記者圈就是會被開這些玩笑。即使感到委屈，你都必須忍受，因為你是一個新人。
有一次，我在立法會完成工作回到大樓記者室，有位攝影師同事扯開嗓子說：「嘩，你像個魚蛋妹（性工作者），如果你是我女兒，我早就打你了。」我不知道當下有多人聽見，有人看了過來，但沒有人出聲。我覺得很受侮辱。
回公司的路上，我和一位要好的男同事吐苦水，說自己真的受不了他。但因為從來沒有人跟我講過，他們也覺得這樣是有問題，所以同一時間，我心裡又會替這位攝影師想藉口：不知道是不是他和女兒有什麼糾紛呢？自己會特別內耗。
況且發聲也不一定有用。有一次，我到國外出差，需要找一個「中間人」牽線。我們約了一頓飯，席間他一直對我毛手毛腳，但因為他能幫我聯絡上需要的人，我只好陪笑。
當時他叫上了一位當地記者出席。在拍照那一刻，他突然抱住我的肩膀，一下子親到我的臉上。我從沒遇過這種情況，嚇到完全說不出話來。同行的攝影記者沒有幫忙，反而跟着一起拍。
離開以後，我馬上私訊編輯。他僅回覆我：「這個地方的人可能是這樣子的，你小心一點。」
小心？我可以小心什麼呢？回來之後，我再跟老闆多講一次，說如果下次有同樣場合，可以找男記者去嗎？老闆說，如果你想，是OK的，但最好還是你去。
我覺得我不被理解、沒有被共情。但我無法理解這種落差——他們經常教我東西，又對我很好，為何卻在騷擾面前，他們好像見慣不怪、只想冷處理？
外界常常覺得記者很堅強、不會軟弱。如果我們被人欺負了，他們會反問：「你不是記者嗎？怎麼自己不出聲呢？」但其實我也只是一個普通人，我們也會有情緒有創傷。更何況我們的圈子很小，我不知道該不該講、也不知該如何講，最後只好自己消化。
不過，現在的我已經學會反駁了。
有部分原因是因為自己長大，也許在這一行做久之後，也開始覺得自己終於有話語權。
當然，社會風氣也有在慢慢改變。我在社交平台看到不少人在現實中會幫忙遭偷拍、被非禮的女生。但有時又會覺得，面對冒犯玩笑，界線還是很模糊：很多人都不知道應不應該出聲，也不知道該不該為了你而得罪人。
所以每次有受害人出來發聲，大家都會覺得這人「很勇敢」——我也覺得 Angela 很勇敢。但又會想，「勇敢」其實也意味着有很多人不敢走出來。
我理解，每個人發聲都有成本。就像在我的經歷中，我沒遇到會為我站出來發聲的人。但我想，也許我可以先成為這個人。
既然過去的講性別玩笑的風氣可以形成，那我們這一代也有機會撐開一些空間，形成另一種社會風氣。我希望有一天，不同性別的人都可以自由、自信；在面對冒犯時不用怪責自己，而是可以直斥其非。
「我不知道什麼才算性騷擾」
Yan，20歲，澳門留學台灣大學生
我在大學修讀劇場專業。為了盡早了解舞台的運作，我透過學長找到一份幫忙搭建演唱會舞台的兼職。那是一份體力活，需要爬上爬下、搬箱子，行業裡男性佔絕對多數，比例大約是八比二。
入行都是邊做邊學。天氣很熱，大家都穿短褲，我也跟着穿了一條運動短褲，長度大概只到大腿中間。但我發現，男女生穿短褲面對的目光很不一樣。每次經過那群男性工人，他們都會盯著我雙腿看，令我很不自在。
我聽不懂台語。學長後來轉述給我聽，說這群工人在談論我：「妹妹今天穿短褲，雙腿好漂亮，像網上看到的（女生）一樣。」還有人形容我像「外賣茶」——在台灣，這是性工作者的意思。
我是覺得他們很煩，但我不是那種「一燃即爆」的女生。後來工作時，我只好盡量避免從他們面前經過。
休息時，一名負責管理的女生有私下找我，叫我以後不要穿短褲，說這樣很易受傷，同時隱晦地提醒我，「大家學識水平不是很高」。我聽出了她的弦外之音，也相信她的本意是要保護我。可我覺得怪怪的，為什麼要改變的總是女生？
但其實，我不太理解什麼才真的算是性騷擾。
中學時在澳門，每天早上我都要坐巴士上學。有好些時間，我會看到一個刻意不拉褲鏈的阿叔。他會跟着女學生上車，站在她們身後。
有一次，他站在我後面，身體貼住我的背。我感受到他的體温，心裡湧出一陣不舒服。可能是怕丟臉，我當時不知所措，也無法避開。後來再見到他，我學會站遠一點。
這件事我沒有跟別人說。但有一次，我再次和他搭同一輛巴士。車上有一位學姐，她突然給我遞來手機，手機裡的備忘錄寫着：「小心你後面有個變態佬」。
我當下很震驚，心想：她應該也有經歷這種騷擾吧。但同時無力感襲來：我們只是中學生，面對這種事，除了互相提醒，我們還能做什麼呢？我們其實什麼都做不了。
這段經歷對我影響很大。它好像給我以後不適的感受定下標準：過去，我即使有人觸碰我的身體，我也沒有出聲，那麼現在遇到色情意味的騷擾，好像也算不上什麼。
離開演唱會舞台工作以後，我報讀了一個健身教練課程。教練比我大八年，才28歲。我的身材比較豐滿。第一次見面時，他就說，如果我跟着他訓練，身材就會變得「有點太好了」，「我會受不了的」。
還有一次，我請教他喝酒對身體的影響。教練說自己很少會喝酒，因為知道自己喝完酒性慾會很高漲。他接着說，但也要看對象，身材不好的女性也不OK，但如果是我的話，他肯定會跟我發生關係。
我感到不適，但還是把它當成「一個玩笑」。我怕如果我認真了，會被人覺得開不起玩笑。我乾笑了兩聲，趕緊中止對話。
「黃色玩笑」真的太常見了。經歷多了，我的腦子好像慢慢有了個開關，自動過濾掉不適的感覺。又或者說，我是麻木了。
「我們是可以出聲的」
關小姐（化名），36歲，香港公共關係從業員
我做公關十年了，是直近兩年，我才學習為自己發聲。
我接觸的客戶和公司很廣泛，從學校、美妝、各種消費品到資訊科技都有。正因為這樣，我們面對色情玩笑的機會有很多。
「做PR（公關），穿得那麼密實嗎？」「什麼是PR？夜總會嗎？」又比如我們安排酒店培訓，客人會問：「培訓？是否有人陪瞓（陪睡）先？」在粵語中，「培訓」和「陪睡」同音。
類似的「玩笑」也不只來自男性，女性也會講類似的話。比如面對大客戶，銷售部門的女同事會半開玩笑地提醒：「明天你記得少扣兩個鈕子」、「裙子記得短一點」。
我明白她是想我們落力一點，但每次聽到這些話我都會反白眼，心想：什麼東西啊？久而久之，我都慢慢消化了。我們工作很忙，如果再要花時間處理這些玩笑，實在太累了。後來就會覺得，算了。
更何況我們做公關的，職責就是跟人建立關係——指出別人的不是，不就等於打破關係嗎？如果剛剛入行不久、職位較低，連做錯事都會怕被人解僱，就更加不敢把這些事講出來。
我曾經遇過一位自己以為關係不錯的記者。在一次完成專訪以後，他突然挽着我手臂，說要跟我「拍拖拖」。公司從沒有教過我們該如何應對這種狀況，我整個人立馬僵硬，不懂反應。我找機會先鬆開他的手，再刻意提起男朋友。我想暗示他：我是有男朋友的，請你不要再碰我。
事後我不斷思忖，為什麼我當下不能直接拒絕他？第一，我真的很害怕。第二，我怕以後的訪問報導很難刊登、見面會很尷尬。一輪覆盤過後，我就會轉過來怪自己了——明明感到不舒服了，為什麼要這樣委屈自己？
做公關，我們習慣做事說話都要包裝、講求圓滑。又有一次，活動結束後趕着發新聞稿，我請客人和我一起在電腦前確認照片。他突然說：「照片這麼隨意被別人看嗎？不會是什麼私密照吧？」
我當下很生氣，臉色立刻沉了下來，這句話真的很過分。但我還要保持禮貌跟客人說：「我不喜歡你說話的方式，請你尊重」。那客人裝作聽不到，事件也就這樣過去了。
其實我有想過要他道歉，但事情不是那麼簡單。很多時候冒犯發生得很快，當下如果沒有立即反應，時機就過了。出來工作以後，首先考慮的通常都不是自己的感受，而是會不會得罪客人、連累同事。這是很難過的事。
直到近兩年，社會經驗多了，我開始學習多愛自己一點，遇到不合理的事就要去反抗。社會風氣也改變了，我看到越來越多是互相聲援被人騷擾的女性，就像最近大家都稱自己是「Jane Doe」一樣，我很受感動。
還有，Gen Z 也有影響到我。人們常說「00後整頓職場」，我覺得是真的！他們界線分明，懂得說不。我才發現原來勇敢說出來，才會爭取到想要的東西。
現在自己懂得分辨哪些算是冒犯的玩笑，如果我看到下屬因為這些說話難堪，我也會指出來。當然，出聲未必會得到想要的結果。但至少出了聲，對方有所收斂，已經能讓我感到舒服一點、釋懷一些。
用玩笑包裝，把「試底線」合理化
根據香港平等機會委員會《2021年全港性騷擾調查》結果，在3,928名受訪者中，有接近12%在過去兩年曾遭職場性騷擾，最常見的形式是「有關性的話題或笑話」。
台灣勞動部則在2026年公布《職場就業平等調查》， 顯示在4,802名女性受訪者中，有3.3%人在過去一年遭受職場性騷擾；當中超過一半人沒有提出申訴，主因是把事件「當開玩笑」。
香港「Anti 480」反性暴力資源中心資深教育主任尹智豪向BBC中文表示，男性和女性同樣均會受到性別言語騷擾，取笑的方向和承受的壓力有所不同——女性較多集中在身材、外貌，以及牽連性騷擾的玩笑。而男性較多面對有關男子氣概、性別氣質的玩笑。
尹智豪指出，「玩笑」很常是言語冒犯者把「試底線」合理化的方法，「試下某個人的底線可以去到哪裡，如果那個人反抗，就（以玩笑作）藉口將責任推回受害者身上」。
他強調，即使言語騷擾沒有對受害者造成身體直接傷害，但受害者也會因為無法脫離共同社交圈子，以及擔心冒犯持續發生而承受精神和社交壓力。
尹智豪指出，性騷擾深受社會文化形塑，比起單靠當事人發聲拒絕，若身旁的人能主動幫忙制止，或身處的企業學校等環境主動建立應對機制，同會有助改變文化。

items.title: 美國下令政府系統禁用DeepSeek：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
items.description: DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。
items.content:
美國下令政府系統禁用DeepSeek：中美AI競爭繼續升溫
  - Author, 卡莉·海斯（Kali Hays）
  - Role, 科技記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 2 分鐘
美國已下令將中國企業深度求索（DeepSeek）的所有人工智能（AI）技術從大多數政府系統中移除。
美國國土安全部（Department of Homeland Security，DHS）已禁止民用政府機構使用深度求索，以及借助其AI模型開發的任何技術。
作為一款功能強大且開源的AI模型，DeepSeek可免費部署，且使用成本較低，因此一直被視為當前AI技術競賽中的顛覆性力量。
雖然國土安全部的通知未詳述圍繞DeepSeek的具體安全疑慮，但白宮今年曾批評來自中國的AI企業。
BBC已聯繫國土安全部、DeepSeek以及中國駐美國大使館請求回應。
國土安全部於週一（10月19日）公布這項命令，但禁令自7月底起已開始生效。
該命令適用於民用機構，包括財政部、國務院及司法部，但國防部轄下機構不在此限。
這項禁令出台之前，特朗普政府及美國企業已對中國的AI提出批評。
白宮科技主管麥可·克拉齊奧斯（Michael Kratsios）今年稍早在一份內部備忘錄中寫道，美國AI企業一直遭到「惡意利用」，主要來自中國的競爭對手企業。
Anthropic與OpenAI都預計在未來數月內於公開市場上市。兩家公司也聲稱，包括DeepSeek在內的一些中國AI企業，實際上複製了它們的AI模型。
美國總統唐納·特朗普（Donald Trump）已明確表示，在AI發展方面，他認為中國是美國的主要競爭對手，而他認為這對美國未來至關重要。
自2025年首次公開推出以來，DeepSeek的人氣持續上升，其模型需求旺盛，甚至一度導致公司伺服器宕機。
DeepSeek的免費聊天機器人應用程式在Apple App Store下載排行榜上名列前茅，其AI模型也被美國科技企業採用。Snowflake、Vercel及OpenRouter等公司都已將DeepSeek整合至其提供給客戶的服務中。
初創企業也紛紛採用像DeepSeek這樣的開源模型。
對科技公司或AI開發者而言，在工作中使用DeepSeek的成本，只是Google Gemini、Anthropic Claude或OpenAI Codex等閉源模型的一小部分。
同樣地，DeepSeek開發其模型所承擔的成本，也遠低於美國AI企業開發自家模型所投入的資金。
去年，DeepSeek表示，訓練其首個版本模型約花費600萬美元，而OpenAI GPT-4相關成本約為1億美元。這些披露令科技股大幅下跌。
DeepSeek最新版本於上週發布。該模型的用戶在網上對其讚譽有加，稱在電腦軟件編程等AI工具的常見任務上，它甚至勝過OpenAI最先進的AI工具。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 法國騷亂：巴黎局部宵禁 被劫商品現身二手平台
items.description: 此前，法國內政部長承認，警方在一些城市「失去了控制」。
items.content:
法國騷亂：巴黎局部宵禁 被劫商品現身二手平台
  - Author, 雅羅斯拉夫·盧基夫（Jaroslav Lukiv）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
法國多地上週末爆發騷亂及搶掠，當局其後在巴黎市中心部分地區及其他城市實施夜間宵禁。
巴黎警方表示，宵禁將於當地時間23:00（格林尼治時間21:00）至06:00期間執行，涉及週末曾有示威者聚集的共和廣場（Place de la République）以及大堂區（Les Halles）購物區。
市中心其他多個地區亦禁止未經批准的集會。
南部城市包括馬賽（Marseille）、波爾多（Bordeaux）、尼斯（Nice）及里昂（Lyon），以及北部的里爾（Lille）及其他城鎮先後宣佈局部宵禁，以及不同程度地限制年輕人出行和集會。
較早前，內政部長洛朗·努涅茲（Laurent Nuñez）承認警方在部分城市「失去控制」。他因騷亂應對準備不足而遭到反對派政客猛烈批評，惟其辭呈被總統馬克龍（Emmanuel Macron）拒絕。
抗議活動始於上月，最初由學生發起，要求改善學校環境，但其後已升級至涵蓋更廣泛的訴求。本週末的示威人數因工會及各類抗議團體加入而增加。
官員表示，已有超過2,500人被捕。據法新社（AFP）報道，一名示威者的手被警方的鎮暴手榴彈炸斷。約1,000名警員受傷。
週一（10月19日）召開危機會議後，總理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科爾尼（Sébastien Lecornu）表示，各地市長將獲授權在「有需要的地方」實施宵禁，但未有指明宵禁將在哪些城市執行。
勒科爾尼並未排除在全國實施緊急狀態的可能。他表示，政府亦將撥款協助受影響地區從破壞中復原，而有關費用將向暴力事件幕後人士追討。
勒科爾尼說：「將會有一項法律出台，設法確保破壞財物的人必須支付賠償。」
他亦宣佈設立部分失業援助基金，幫助因騷亂及搶掠而無法工作的人。
與此同時，努涅茲表示，200名調查人員正在分析閉路電視片段，試圖找出可能的主謀。
他週日（18日）曾提出辭職，但遭馬克龍拒絕。愛麗舍宮（Élysée Palace）表示，理由是「基於執法部門指揮工作延續性的需要」。
聲明稱，努涅茲應就馬克龍所稱的「情報及預見性失誤」保持透明。
法國工商會（CCI）主席阿蘭·迪克雷森佐（Alain Di Crescenzo）表示，超過2,000間商店及其他商戶直接受到週末暴力事件影響。
迪克雷森佐向盧森堡廣播電視公司（RTL）法國分台表示，騷亂造成的損失估計達「數億歐元」。
工商會馬賽分會主席讓—呂克·紹萬（Jean-Luc Chauvin）向BBC表示，該市許多店主陷入「極度困境」，擔心生計不保。
兩名法國政府部長表示，被搶掠的物品已在部分銷售平台上架。二手交易平台 Vinted 的發言人表示，出售或兜售贓物屬「嚴格禁止」行為。
該公司說：「自本週末以來，我們的團隊已立即採取行動，識別並移除與搶掠有關的商品，並加強對可疑商品的監察。」
約55萬名示威者於週末走上街頭，抗議燃油價格上漲、生活成本上升，以及包括學校在內的公共服務惡化。
在巴黎、馬賽及其他城市和較小城鎮，有身穿黑衣、戴上口罩及面罩的騷亂者縱火焚燒汽車和建築物，並搶掠商戶。
在中部城市利摩日（Limoges），裝飾華麗的19世紀市政廳於上週六（17日）被騷亂者縱火焚毀，鐘樓及屋頂在火勢蔓延中倒塌。
美國駐法國大使館發出警示，建議公民避開近期受示威影響的地區。
警示呼籲公民若身處大型集會附近應「保持謹慎」。中國及德國亦發出了類似警告。
部分政客指控左翼政黨「不屈法國」（La France Insoumise, LFI）在暴力事件中扮演角色。勒科爾尼在較早前的記者會上更指，某些團體「想在我國製造混亂，直至總統大選」。
該黨領袖梅朗雄（Jean-Luc Mélenchon）將角逐明年總統選舉，他回應時要求法國總理「證明其指控」，否則就要「道歉、閉嘴，並停止煽動動亂」。

items.title: 投资德国峰会斩逾2250亿欧元承诺 默茨以“可预测”德国人形象招商
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/投资德国峰会斩逾2250亿欧元承诺-默茨以-可预测-德国人形象招商/a-79715886?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 柏林投资德国峰会上,德国经济部长表示迄今已有逾2250亿欧元的投资承诺。电商巨头亚马逊计划于2027年向德国投资160亿欧元；德国政府宣布与英伟达深化AI合作。但近年来德国吸引外资面临挑战，能源价格高企和劳动力成本仍是投资者顾虑因素。
items.content:
投资德国峰会斩逾2250亿欧元承诺 默茨以“可靠的”德国人形象招商
2026年10月20日
（德国之声中文网）德国经济部长赖歇（Katherina Reiche）周二（10月20日）表示, 在柏林举行的投资德国峰会上，德国迄今已获得超过2250亿欧元的投资承诺。此次峰会吸引了众多商界领袖参加。
赖歇没有透露已达成承诺的具体细节, 但她对德国广播电台(Deutschlandfunk)表示,这一数字只统计了金额超过1亿欧元的交易。
计划向德国投资的企业包括在线零售巨头亚马逊。该公司表示，计划于明年在德国投入约160亿欧元，用于多个项目。
亚马逊表示，这些投资将包括“扩建数据中心和AI基础设施、通过Amazon Leo提供高速卫星互联网服务、在德国各地开展新的物流项目,以及为Prime Video大幅增加新制作内容”。
亚马逊首席全球事务与法务官戴维·扎波尔斯基（David Zapolsky）在一份声明中说:“德国是创新中心,也是欧洲最具吸引力的投资目的地之一。”
他表示：“这就是为什么我们自2010年以来在德国投资超过1000亿欧元，以及为什么计划在2027年追加投资160亿欧元的原因。我们希望德国企业、社区和创作者能够拥有所需的基础设施和工具，以增强竞争力、实现增长。”
默茨夸德国人“可靠、可预测”为招商引资造势
德国总理默茨发表开幕演讲并表示：“德国对商业投资敞开大门。”
峰会上,德国总理默茨为把德国塑造成理想的营商之地,大谈德国和德国人的各种常见刻板印象。
“德国人勤劳,早睡,天不亮就起床, 最堵的时间是早上6点到7点。"
“假期里，我们总是最早到达海滩，早餐前就把毛巾铺好。如果我们约定了交货日期，就一定会遵守。如果你邀请德国朋友晚上7点来吃饭，我们会在6点58分到达。”
“我们可靠、可预测、严谨,而且不会让人意外,”默茨说道,”简而言之,我们正是投资者最青睐的那种人。"
财政部长克林拜尔在向潜在投资者喊话时同样用了直白的幽默:” 我想要你们的钱。"
二人的推介看来都奏效了——峰会期间达成了数千亿欧元规模的投资承诺。
“欧洲如何监管AI？”“若无技术,监管无从谈起”
峰会期间，德国与美国科技巨头英伟达（Nvidia）达成协议，将深化双方在人工智能领域的合作，推动人工智能技术在德国工业中的应用。
默茨与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋表示,德国的工程技术专长与前沿AI技术相结合,将有助于长期增强德国经济实力。
值得一提的是，默茨在与黄仁勋举行的同台对谈中发问“欧洲应如何监管AI？”后者直言答道：“如果技术不存在，就无从监管。”黄仁勋认为，产业必须研发出安全技术，再建立具约束力的标准，最后才是政府与产业制定规范，如果AI产业无法蓬勃发展，“那就没什么可监管的”。
德国吸引外资优势与挑战并存
超过200名来自德国及国际大型企业、投资银行和投资基金的高管参加了此次峰会。周二，峰会还安排了闭门会谈。
峰会旨在吸引外国资本投资德国。主办方着重强调德国的公共财政稳健、信用评级为最高的AAA级、法治体系健全，以及在欧洲专利申请方面处于领先地位。德国是七国集团（G7）中唯一保有AAA主权信用评级的国家。
尽管具备这些优势，近年来德国在吸引外国投资方面仍面临困难。能源价格高企和劳动力成本上升，成为阻碍投资的因素。
德国政府方面表示，在政府寻求改善基础设施、支持企业向气候中和型生产转型之际，私人投资对于弥补公共资金缺口至关重要。

items.title: 德语媒体：不要跌入北京的贸易陷阱
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：不要跌入北京的贸易陷阱/a-79715211?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 对于北京刚刚出台的技术出口管制新规，《法兰克福汇报》评论写道，北京虽然宣称此举是为了捍卫国家安全，但为未来针对西方的谈判中，增加手中筹码也是不能排除的因素。《日报》评论称，欧洲如不尽快提升自身竞争力，今后同北京的“平等合作”将越来越难。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《法兰克福汇报》评论写道，欧盟同中国就限制中国电动车出口数量所达成的协议墨迹未干，北京就推出了新的技术出口限制清单：人工智能、生物科技以及太阳能产品等领域的出口，今后要么全盘禁止，要么需接受严格审查。这篇题为《技术自主》的评论写道：
“北京这一步骤凸显了世界观的不同。在习近平看来，实现技术自主才是重中之重，其背后原因则是19世纪错过工业革命而给中国留下的的历史创伤。在过去的一百多年里，中国一直处于技术落后的地位。
中国从中汲取的历史教训也很简单：要想保持独立和强大，就必须掌握技术。也正因为如此，中国更为偏重理工科教育，每年都会培养出数以百万计的工程师，各级学校里对人工智能的重视程度也远远超过欧洲。中国每年对工业领域的投资之多，更是令人震惊。这样的产业政策也造成了中国经济结构的严重失衡，对于大多数老百姓来说，这更是一场旷日持久的经济危机。”
《法兰克福汇报》的评论指出，中国的产业政策虽然造成了严重的产能过剩，但也暴露了欧洲对华政策的无奈：贸易壁垒或许能暂时保护本土经济，但却无法改变同中国竞争中的被动局面：
“对中国产品征收关税或设置出口上限，或能保障欧洲企业的市场份额，但却无法提升欧洲的技术竞争力，更无法改善欧洲汽车在第三方市场的被动局面。欧洲对华贸易政策虽然能在个别领域产生效果，但它的着眼点却是错误的：它没有正面迎接竞争，而是在助长欧洲的僵化发展。这样的政策只能缓解症状，但却没有找到真正的病因。”
欧洲不应沦为任凭北京摆布的乞求者
《日报》评论指出，“说一套做一套”是中国政府的常态，而一旦涉及国家安全，这种“言行不一”就表现得尤为明显。中国党和国家领导人习近平刚刚在国际舞台上承诺，中国愿意以开明姿态促进技术领域的国际合作。但话音未落，中国就出台了一个长长的关键技术出口管制清单：
“欧洲应当对中国的言行不一高度警觉。过去几十年以来，北京一直都在敦促西方企业转让技术。而现如今，当中国在某些领域占据主导地位之后，却立即开始了系统性的封锁政策。在‘去风险’的问题上，北京的做法也如出一辙：它一边谴责欧洲试图减少对华依赖的尝试，而与此同时，中国却在狂热地追求着这样的目标：不对任何国家产生依赖。
众所周知，在中南海看来，供应链和工业实力首先是政治施压武器。习近平过去几年所追寻的战略就是：本国经济尽可能自给自足，而整个世界则应高度依赖中国产品。
每当政治关系陷入紧张或贸易战一触即发的当口，北京就会不失时机地拿出手中的王牌。其中最著名的例子就是稀土。迄今为止，中国一直在稀土加工方面占据全球垄断地位。即便是在绿色技术领域，中国领导层也一直在为双边合作设定附加条件。
布鲁塞尔和柏林要对中国的所作所为有一个清醒的认识：北京希望将欧洲降格到乞求者的地位，届时欧洲只有满足了北京开出的条件，才会有资格同中国开展合作。

items.title: 美国禁止联邦机构使用“深度求索”
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/美国禁止联邦机构使用-深度求索/a-79715294?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 美国国土安全部发布通告称，使用深度求索可能导致敏感数据流向中国，因此禁止联邦政府部门使用相关产品。中国外交部回应称，反对将经贸政治化。
items.content:
美国禁止联邦机构使用“深度求索”
2026年10月20日
（德国之声中文网）美国政府周一（10月19日）下令联邦机构停止使用中国人工智能工具“深度求索”（DeepSeek）。
美国国土安全部的通告宣布，禁止使用深度求索开发的产品，以及第三方使用深度求索创建的工具。通告称，必须从IT设备中移除相关工具。
周一的这份通告中写道：“深度求索的模型存在多种威胁途径。”
国土安全部警告说，使用深度求索人工智能工具“可能导致敏感数据传输（向中国），倘若美国政府雇员或供应商使用的话”。
该通告说，深度求索的服务器位于中国，该国法律体系下，政府拥有“广泛的权限”访问私有公司的基础设施。
美国曾指责深度求索等中国顶尖的人工智能公司系统性窃取美国公司研发的先进模型能力。
尽管中美在AI领域面临激烈竞争，9月，两国间仍达成一致，设立人工智能领域的对话机制。
预计该议题也将出现在下月美中领导人会晤的日程上。11月中旬，美国总统特朗普与中国国家主席习近平预计将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会期间举行会晤。
“大量个人数据存储在中国”
周二，中国外交部发言人在被问及此事时表示：“中方一贯反对泛化国家安全概念、将科技经贸问题政治化。我们将坚决维护中国企业合法权益。”
路透社写道，按照深度求索自身的隐私政策，大量个人数据被存储在中国，包括向其AI程序提出的请求，以及上传的文档。除美国外，还有一些国家出于安全隐忧禁用深度求索。
比如澳大利亚。去年2月，澳大利亚在所有政府设备上禁用深度求索，因担忧构成安全风险。捷克去年7月禁止该国公共行政部门使用深度求索的任何服务，原因是担忧数据安全。台湾去年2月禁止政府部门使用深度求索的服务，因视其为安全风险。此外，台湾也就深度求索的审查以及数据流向中国表示忧虑。还有一些国家正在对深度求索的安全性进行审查。
DeepSeek V4 引爆需求：华为升腾950芯片遭各大厂商“疯抢”
（美联社、法新社、路透社）

items.description: 据《华尔街日报》报导，普京希望在深圳APEC期间与特朗普和习近平举行三方会谈。特朗普对这场峰会的可能性持开放态度，但更希望聚焦核武控制，而非乌克兰局势。中国外交部仅称“没有可以提供的信息”。
items.content:
特朗普：愿意举行美中俄峰会 聚焦去核化议题
2026年10月20日
（德国之声中文网）美国总统特朗普周一（10月19日）表示，他愿意与中国国家主席习近平和俄国总统普京会晤。此前，《华尔街日报》消息称普京提议下个月于中国深圳的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会期间举行三方会谈，商议乌克兰局势。不过，据特朗普的说法，他希望谈的议题是核武控制。
“我可以（举行三方会谈）。倒不是为了乌克兰，因为坦白讲，俄罗斯在乌克兰议题表现还行，他们没做什么，中国也是。我们会想谈核武的事，还有去核化。”
特朗普说，如果习近平希望举行这场会谈，那他也愿意安排，“我想我们也会谈到其他议题，例如贸易”。
有媒体追问，这场三方会谈究竟是否谈及乌克兰，特朗普称他会尽自己所能终结俄乌战争。
近期美国与乌克兰关系恶化，乌克兰总统泽连斯基公开质疑美方故意拖延交付“爱国者”拦截飞弹，而且不分享战场情资给乌克兰。与此同时，美俄之间越走越近，特朗普先是与普京达成柴油协议，上周又宣布暂缓实施对俄罗斯的新一波制裁。此举被批评者称是在向普京让步，背弃乌克兰及欧洲盟友。泽连斯基则称特朗普“站在历史错误的一方”。
19日，特朗普捍卫自己的决策，称泽连斯基“根本不知道自己在说什么”。 “其实我觉得，是时候换其他人来代表乌克兰谈判了。”
面对俄美中三国领袖可能在排除乌克兰的情况下谈俄乌停战，乌克兰外交部长瑟比加（Andriy Sybiga）认为这只会适得其反、鼓舞普京继续这场战争。他说普京是个“战犯”，“从任何务实或道德的观点来看，普京都不应该跟特朗普和习近平同桌而坐”。
克里姆林宫发言人佩斯科夫（Dmitry Peskov）证实三方的确有谈到是否举行会晤，但目前还没有实质的会议提案，也尚未讨论到具体的议程。他还称，如果没有“准备好承担责任”的乌方代表参与，就不可能达成最终的停战协议。
中国外交部发言人毛宁也被问及三方会谈的可能性，她仅称“目前没有可以提供的信息”。
潜在三方峰会对北京而言利弊共存
研究中国问题的分析人士对《华尔街日报》指出，若三方对话在中国举行，对习近平而言，将是提升中国作为外交斡旋力量地位迈出的一大步。华盛顿智库史汀生中心中国项目主任孙韵对该报表示：“中国希望被视为大国之间的枢纽，并有可能成为美国与俄罗斯之间的调解方。”
但也有分析人士认为，三方对话对北京而言也并非毫无弊处：若三国对话在APEC峰会期间举行，中国方面也担心，这场会谈可能喧宾夺主，冲淡北京借助峰会展示自身在亚太地区影响力的计划。分析人士还称习近平正试图在支持普京与维护对欧洲关之间维持谨慎平衡。此种三方会晤也可能使中国更直接地卷入乌克兰战争，并引发欧洲国家的反弹。
美国中期选举在即 与莫斯科关系出现转向
该报随后援引一名了解相关情况的俄罗斯前情报官员的话报道称，普京是在10月9日与特朗普的一次电话交谈中提出了这一想法。两国之间的柴油交易也是在此次通话中达成的。
特朗普于同一日宣布同意俄罗斯向美国和全球市场供应俄罗斯柴油，以期降低全球能源价格。
分析人士对路透社指出，美国中期选举临近，且美国民众已因美以伊战争等因素导致的生活成本上升而承压。若对俄制裁生效，可能进一步推高油价，从而对共和党中期选举的选情造成不利影响。
特朗普对泽连斯基不满
上周日（10月18日）俄罗斯发布消息称圣彼得堡遭到大规模乌克兰无人机袭击。袭击发生后，特朗普在社交媒体平台Truth Social上发文批评泽连斯基将俄罗斯柴油炼油厂作为打击目标。“他很清楚这些袭击严重损害了全球柴油市场，也波及到了美国”，特朗普称其“根本不想结束这场战争，而且他可能从一开始就不想结束”。
特朗普还为其暂缓制裁俄罗斯的决定解释缘由，称“不希望采取任何可能导致俄罗斯愚蠢地退出谈判桌的行动”。
《华尔街日报》分析称，莫斯科认为潜在的美中俄三方对话有助于巩固俄罗斯作为全球大国俱乐部成员的地位。这种会谈形式还将欧洲排除在外，克里姆林宫视欧洲为俄罗斯在乌克兰取得胜利的主要障碍。该报引述俄罗斯前情报官员的话写道，普京对这种三方会谈机制抱有宏大、但并不现实的设想，希望将其打造为第二次“雅尔塔会议”。
将乌克兰排除在外或为台海问题释放信号
《华尔街日报》进一步分析若美中俄三国领导人共同商讨乌克兰问题，会谈却不邀请乌克兰参加，将开创前所未有的先例，并引发欧洲及其他地区的警觉，比如人们可能加剧这样一种担忧，即台湾有朝一日，尤其是中国未放弃武统的背景下，也可能在类似的场合被拿来谈判。

items.title: 法国宣布实施局部宵禁 暴力骚乱蔓延至欧洲多国
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/法国宣布实施局部宵禁-暴力骚乱蔓延至欧洲多国/a-79714138?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 法国政府周一宣布在巴黎及其他部分地区实施局部宵禁，同时未排除宣布进入紧急状态的可能。此前，因物价飞涨而引发的示威活动演变成全国骚乱。与此同时，暴力抗议活动在欧洲各地蔓延。
items.content:
法国宣布实施局部宵禁 暴力骚乱蔓延至欧洲多国
2026年10月20日
（德国之声中文网）上周六，法国全国约50万人走上街头抗议生活成本飙升。这是持续四周抗议活动的一次集中爆发。最初和平的示威活动随后在多个城市演变成暴力冲突。蒙面人群袭击执法人员、闯入公共建筑纵火，抢劫商店，焚烧汽车、自行车和电动滑板车。
法国政府于周一晚间在多个城镇实施了宵禁。当局宣布从周一晚间至周二早晨，巴黎、里尔和里昂等多个城市将实施部分宵禁，以保护商业场所。
巴黎宵禁从当地时间晚间11点生效，示威活动则从晚上8时起被禁止。巴黎共和国广场（Place de la République）和莱阿勒（Les Halles）购物区实施宵禁，规定任何人不得进入或在这两个区域内逗留。
法国北部里尔、杜埃、德南和瓦蒂尼等地将在未来两日对未成年人实施宵禁，时间为晚上8时至次日早上6时。
法国南部尼斯等地实施宵禁，其中尼斯市中心专门针对未成年人实施宵禁。
法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔尼（Sebastien Lecornu）周二表示，将在必要地区继续实施新的宵禁，并且不排除宣布进入紧急状态的可能。
面对“未能预见并应对暴力事件”的指责，法国政府誓言要恢复秩序，并努力平息公众的愤怒情绪。
示威者号召更多抗议活动
距法国举行总统选举仅剩六个月，骚乱却有持续蔓延之势。法国工会已呼吁于11月5日再次举行集会。
马克龙将周六发生的骚乱和抢劫归咎于有组织的极左翼团体。
法国政府指责极左翼团体煽动暴力，意图提高极左翼激进政治人物让-吕克·梅朗雄（Jean-Luc Mélenchon）在总统选举中的胜算。
总理勒科尔尼周一在紧急内阁会议后表示，他“已下定决心，全力恢复公共秩序”。法国内政部长此前称警方已经“失去控制”。
勒科尔尼拒绝排除宣布进入紧急状态的可能性。一旦宣布紧急状态，当局将获得广泛权力，以限制公众集会。
二手平台被要求下架“赃物” 超2500人被捕
周一，法国数字事务部长安妮·勒埃南夫（Anne Le Henanff）敦促网络二手交易平台下架骚乱事件中被抢劫的“赃物”，并召集了包括Vinted和eBay在内的多家公司代表进行会谈。
至少有3000家商店遭到破坏，损失金额高达数亿欧元。
司法部长热拉尔·达尔马宁（Gérald Darmanin）表示，自周末以来，全国已有超过2513人被警方拘留，其中67人被监禁，并已立案调查数十起刑事案件。
近1000名安全部队人员受伤，示威者也有人受伤，其中一名示威者的手被警方用于控制人群的手榴弹炸飞。
马克龙承认，政府应对骚乱的措施存在失误。周六，法国共部署了6万名执法人员。
达尔马宁表示，当局将利用社交媒体上的面部识别技术，识别参与暴力事件的人员。
马克龙周日在全国电视讲话中谴责这种“肆无忌惮”的暴力行为。
欧盟称这些暴力行为“不可接受”，但同时警告说，法国必须保护民众和平示威的权利。
暴力骚乱蔓延至欧洲其他国家
欧洲其他国家也出现了因物价上涨引发的示威活动。
意大利安莎通讯社报道称，米兰、都灵和博洛尼亚等城市连续几天针对高生活成本的和平抗议演变成骚乱和抢劫。总理梅洛尼召集紧急内阁会议，讨论应对方案，并考虑实施宵禁。
米兰市中心大教堂广场上，身穿黑衣戴面罩的年轻人砸碎商店橱窗并抢劫超市。官方数据显示，至少14名安全人员受伤。总计有270多人被拘留，其中大多数是未成年人。
米兰检方形容该事件为“罕见的暴力程度”。
米兰市长朱塞佩·萨拉（Giuseppe Sala）表示：“我非常担忧，因为这是一种新现象-起源于国际局势，并会因此而不断滋长。”
阿尔巴尼亚总理埃迪·拉马周一表示，反政府示威者已经越过“红线”。此前的反政府示威期间，警察局遭到纵火。
自上周二以来，阿尔巴尼亚示威者持续与警方发生冲突。此前数月针对大学条件和政治腐败的抗议活动达到了顶峰。
周一晚间，首都地拉那再次发生骚乱。示威者向内政部投掷燃烧弹，防暴警察则使用高压水炮、催泪瓦斯和橡胶子弹予以回应。
据当地政府称，冲突已造成约300人受伤，其中超过一半是警察。警方表示周日地拉那发生的骚乱中，共68人被拘留，其中22人将面临刑事起诉。
在比利时，警方在布鲁塞尔和列日使用催泪瓦斯和高压水炮驱散示威者。
在西班牙，抗议者在马德里市中心搭起帐篷，谴责住房成本飙升。
邻国葡萄牙的主要城市里斯本和波尔图也出现了类似的露营抗议活动。

items.title: Two re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran intelligence after RAF Fairford incident
items.description: The head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing said they consider Iranian state involvement "highly likely".
items.content:
Two re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran intelligence after RAF Fairford incident
- Published
Two men have been re-arrested after an incident near RAF Fairford last month, counter-terrorism police have said.
A 24-year-old UK national, and a 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national, are being held on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service under Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023, with police saying the investigation relates to Iran.
Police had been alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the US airbase in Gloucestershire in the early hours of 27 September - a major incident was subsequently declared and dozens of homes evacuated.
Seven men in total have been arrested as part of the counter-terror police investigation.
Gloucestershire Police said it had received a call about "three suspicious vehicles" travelling towards RAF Fairford at 00:45 BST on 27 September.
A bomb disposal team was deployed to the village to examine a number of vehicles.
Petrol was found in three vans near the airbase and five men were arrested.
They had been initially arrested on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and then further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.
Police later said they did not find "improvised explosive devices".
The re-arrests announced on Tuesday relate to a 24-year-old man who was initially arrested on 27 September near the base and a 25-year-old who was arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts days later on 1 October in the borough of Westminster.
The other five men - who also include a 22-year-old British national arrested in Westminster on 6 October - remain on police bail.
The head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said: "This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement.
"Our investigators are continuing to examine what that level of involvement was and the ambition behind it."
The officer added that national security investigations can take time to progress due to their sensitive nature.
"Our specialist teams have been working tirelessly to interrogate the many lines of enquiry involved in this hugely complex investigation," he said.
Days after the incident, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC there were "strong indications" Iran had played a part in the incident.
He did not provide further details at the time.
Iran has previously denied any involvement.
RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for Fairford to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.
In the week after the incident, it emerged that the US had pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.
US President Donald Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base without giving specific details.

items.title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds
items.description: The sixth report from Covid inquiry criticises the lack of PPE and the way patients were discharged from hospital.
items.content:
Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds
- Published
Government failures in care settings created an environment that allowed Covid to spread like wildfire, an official inquiry has said.
The sixth report from the Covid inquiry said the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought" in the early stages of the pandemic and there was no "protective ring" put around homes as claimed by ministers at the time.
There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
The 287-page report also highlighted shortages of PPE for carers and criticised the way hospital patients were discharged into care homes.
It said limits on visits caused enormous harm to residents and their loved ones, though it blamed this on care homes themselves.
Around 1.5 million adults were either living in care homes or receiving support in their own homes when Covid hit.
Action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences, the inquiry said.
Chair Baroness Hallet said a lack of testing, PPE and pre-pandemic planning combined with policy decisions early on "created an environment in which the virus could spread like wildfire".
"At the critical early stages of the pandemic, not enough was done to protect those living and working in care homes," she said.
"The overriding focus of the UK government and devolved administrations was on protecting hospitals."
- Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says 
  - Published7 hours ago
- Covid inquiry PPE report - key findings 
  - Published14 July
Lack of PPE and financial support for carers
At the start of the pandemic, the then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock said the government had placed a protective ring around care homes.
But the report said that this claim was unfounded.
It also found:
- a lack of PPE meant staff had to resort to make-shift workarounds, including bins bags, festival waterproof ponchos and painters' overalls
- the decision to discharge hospitals patients into care homes at the start of the pandemic was understandable, but guidance should have made clear they needed to be isolated. This did not happen in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, which was a significant oversight
- a lack of financial support for care workers at the start of the pandemic made it difficult to allow them to stay away from their job if they were infected
- long-standing weakness in the care sector, including financial struggles and staff shortages, exacerbated problems
- by September 2020, evidence suggested care home visitors posed only a marginal infection risk, yet many care homes failed to ease restrictions in line with updated UK guidance, contributing to a significant decline in residents' health and wellbeing.
- there was evidence of blanket do-not-resuscitate orders being put in place in some care homes, which is considered unlawful
- millions of unpaid carers were left to take on evermore complex care and struggled because of a lack of support
Jean Adamson, of the Covid-19 Bereaved Families for Justice UK, said: "Today's report is a devastating account of one of the darkest episodes in our country's history.
"It shows that the government knew the care sector was extremely vulnerable to a pandemic and yet did nothing. Failing to act until it was too late."
Totally exposed
Caroline, Abrahams, the charity director at Age UK, said the report was "devastating".
"When Covid took off, people using social care and the staff and unpaid carers providing it were left totally exposed."
She added it also demonstrated how important the overhaul of social care promised by Andy Burnham when he became prime minister was.
"If a national care service had already been in place... the various disasters that befell social care during the pandemic would have been lessened and some might have been avoided altogether."
Meanwhile, Natalie Grayson, from the GMB union, said care workers were "left vulnerable and terribly exposed" during the pandemic which saw "care homes turned into morgues".
"That cannot be allowed to happen again," she added.
Nadra Ahmed, co-chair of the National Care Association, which represents care providers in England described the findings as "really upsetting", adding that the social care workforce has "never fully recovered" from the pandemic.
She said we need to "start thinking about social care in a more constructive way" and the mantra that "we all had to protect the NHS" appears to have come at the cost of "some care home residents' lives".
Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government would provide a "full response" to the report's recommendations "in due course".
Speaking in the Commons, Cooper said she agreed that social care had been "undervalued and under-recognised" for too long.
"My thoughts are with all those who lost loved ones in the pandemic, and especially those who endured the immense distress and harm of visiting restrictions in care homes, which meant they could not be with loved ones even as they died," she added.

items.title: Google resolves cloud outage affecting UK banks and websites
items.description: Revolut was one of the hardest hit, with banking services going down for many customers.
items.content:
Google resolves cloud outage affecting UK banks and websites
- Published
Google Cloud says it has resolved disruption at its UK cloud site which caused an outage affecting UK banks, businesses and the courts.
The company, one of a few large cloud computing firms whose infrastructure and services underpin many online platforms, reported an "issue with multiple services" at its London data centre complex "europe-west2" early on Tuesday.
Revolut, Lloyds Bank and HSBC were among popular UK services that confirmed disruption on Tuesday morning, after thousands of reports of problems were raised by users online.
The tech giant apologised to those affected and thanked customers for their patience.
"We have resolved a disruption to Google Cloud services at a third-party facility in our europe-west2 cloud region due to a power event," a Google Cloud spokesperson said in a statement on Tuesday evening.
"Services have been restored."
They added that the company would publish an analysis of the incident on its service health dashboard, external, where it provides customers with updates about the status of its cloud services globally.
Cloud computing giants like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud make their services available to clients in local or regional sites around the world, which they call "regions", containing their data centres.
In updates to its service dashboard on Tuesday morning, Google Cloud had said a number of its cloud services were "experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region" - its UK cloud facility in London.
It later said that the issues had stemmed from a "power event" within one of its smaller data centre zones, europe-west2-b.
These seemingly affected a host of popular UK platforms and services, with customers flagging issues with sites including Royal Mail, DPD and e-bike service Forest.
The HM Courts and Tribunals Service also said it was aware of an issue affecting the video platform used for remote hearings.
Banking services disrupted
Banks appeared to be among the most badly affected, with customers reporting problems ranging from being unable to access funds abroad to struggling to complete a property purchase.
Rachael Ellen, 25, a Revolut customer from Glasgow, told BBC News she was left unable to access her money.
"Today I was unable to pay for my parking at a shopping centre because my Revolut account wasn't working properly," she told the BBC.
"This left me in a difficult situation as I had no way to access the money I needed at the time."
She said the outage also meant she could not view a transaction from a relative and was told by the app's help bot that there were no pending incoming transactions.
"It's frustrating not knowing where the payment is or when I'll receive it," Rachael added.
More than 1,500 reports of issues affecting Revolut services were flagged to platform outage monitor shortly after 08:00 BST on Tuesday.
A spokesperson for the company said some Revolut services were disrupted earlier as a result of the Google Cloud outage.
"We can confirm that services are now fully restored. Our customers' money and data are safe and remained safe throughout.
"We apologise for any inconvenience caused."
Customers of Lloyds Bank, Halifax and Bank of Scotland - all owned by the Lloyds Banking Group - also reported issues affecting some online banking services.
A Lloyds spokesperson did not confirm the cause of issues affecting some of its services, but told the BBC later on Tuesday "we understand the root issues have been resolved, so we expect all our services to be back to normal soon".
'Incredibly frustrating'
Guy Baybutt, who works for a family-run business The Veg Box Company also said he was "severely affected" by Tuesday's outage.
Baybutt, who is from Preston, told the BBC the firm - which supplies fresh fruit, vegetables and other produce to customers across the UK - could not access its website to download and process customer orders amid the technical issues.
"We were also unable to book parcels onto DPD's system for collection, meaning orders that should have been dispatched today were at risk of being delayed," he said.
"To make matters worse, customers were unable to access our website to place new orders, meaning we lost valuable sales during the outage."
He said that such disruptions can have "serious financial consequences" for small businesses like his own.
"We don't have the resources of larger companies to simply absorb lost revenue, particularly when we're dealing with fresh, perishable produce that needs to reach customers promptly," Baybutt added.
Dependent on the cloud
Tuesday's incident came exactly one year after more than 1,000 sites, including UK banks, were knocked offline for hours during an outage at AWS' largest cloud site.
Experts say this latest outage show how many businesses still rely on core services provided by a few large cloud operators.
"Google Cloud's outage is a reminder of how deeply our economies depend on just a handful of cloud providers," said Prof Feng Li, associate dean for research & innovation at Bayes Business School.
He added that it was not yet clear what caused the power problem identified by Google Cloud.
"Large cloud systems are complex, and failures will happen.
"What matters is how far they spread, how quickly services recover and whether customers have workable alternatives," he added.

items.title: BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close
items.description: The closures are announced as the corporation continues to try to save £500m over two years.
items.content:
BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close
- Published
The BBC is to close its BBC Three and BBC Scotland television channels in the spring, as the corporation continues to make £500m of savings over two years.
Both services will become online-only, meaning they will continue to produce and host some content on iPlayer, without the need to fill a terrestrial TV schedule.
The BBC has also announced the closure of Radio 4 Extra, which largely airs speech programmes from the BBC's archive, including comedy, drama and documentaries.
BBC director-general Matt Brittin said: "We need to make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world. We all know that means tough choices."
Discussing the closure of linear broadcast services, Brittin said: "Much of the great content they currently carry will still be found where audiences already enjoy them on iPlayer and Sounds.
"While this follows media speculation, I recognise the confirmation of this news will be hard for audiences and colleagues."
Outlining the plans, the corporation confirmed:
- BBC Scotland will remain a channel on iPlayer, with some content also broadcast on BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland
- BBC Three commissions, supported by increased investment in content for younger audiences, will be available on BBC iPlayer and on other platforms including YouTube
- Some programmes that air on Radio 4 Extra will be available on BBC Sounds - while its religious programme The Daily Service will be on BBC Sounds and local radio
BBC Three, which is aimed at young audiences and launched hits such as Fleabag, Normal People and Gavin & Stacey, previously moved online in 2016, but was reinstated as a TV channel in 2022.
BBC Scotland launched as a channel in 2019, broadcasting a variety of Scottish programming including news, sport, documentaries and entertainment.
However, some of the shows that air on the two networks, such as Two Doors Down on BBC Scotland and Sort Your Life Out on BBC Three, are repeats of episodes originally broadcast on other more mainstream BBC channels.
Both networks currently only broadcast TV programming in the evenings, although BBC Scotland simulcasts BBC Radio Scotland during the rest of the day.
The BBC said that the network's nightly programme Reporting Scotland: News at Seven will not move to BBC iPlayer and will cease when the linear channel closes.
Audiences will continue to be served by BBC Scotland's wider news offering, including Reporting Scotland, The Sunday Show, Radio Scotland Breakfast, Debate Night and Scotcast, the corporation said.
While Radio 4 Extra does air some original programming, its schedule is predominantly made up of archive content, much of which is available on BBC Sounds.
Sir Peter Bazalgette, former chairman of ITV and production company Endemol, told BBC News: "This is a modest and pretty well-judged package.
"The essence of it is it protects the spending on content, it really cuts money in the distribution of programmes, and it really had to happen because the BBC has lost 30% of its revenue in 10 years."
But entertainment trade union Equity said Tuesday's announcement "does not signal a thriving BBC, and we are concerned about the UK's preeminent public service broadcaster's ability to meet its duties to the fullest".
Affected staff were told about the changes on Tuesday, although the proposed closure of BBC Scotland and BBC Three had been reported by some media outlets in recent weeks.
The BBC is aiming to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs - almost one in 10 - in an attempt to save £500m over two years as it faces "significant financial pressures".
Around 550 job closures have already been announced in news, while more than 30 job cuts have so far been announced for BBC Sport.
The newly appointed director of BBC News, Rachel Jupp, announced on Tuesday that a further £5.5m of savings were being proposed, which would represent the closure of around 100 roles.
Meanwhile, several high-profile BBC TV series have been cancelled altogether in recent weeks.
RuPaul's Drag Race UK, Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, Live at the Apollo, Football Focus, Ski Sunday and Radio 4’s The World Tonight and You & Yours are among the programmes the BBC has dropped so far.

items.title: Harry says he wants to 'reconcile' with his family
items.description: Prince Harry says he wants reconciliation with his family, in an interview with a magazine in New York last month.
items.content:
Harry says he wants to 'reconcile' with his family
- Published
The Duke of Sussex has said he wants to repair his complicated relationships with his father and brother, in a magazine interview.
"Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile - that's the key point," Prince Harry told GQ in New York.
"Scars stick around forever. But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past, that's something that I would encourage everybody to do," said Prince Harry.
Last week Prince Harry and Meghan carried out their first public engagement together since their return to the UK in the summer.
The GQ interview with Prince Harry was conducted last month and released as the Royal Family were on duty in Windsor welcoming the Sultan of Oman at the start of a state visit.
But a spokesman for the Sussexes said the interview was recorded in late September and it was the entirely the publishers' decision when to run it - and that nothing should be read into the timing.
The spokesman also said that the reference to "some people don't want it to work out" was not a swipe at his brother Prince William or any other member of his family.
Prince Harry and Meghan moved from the UK to the United States in 2020, stepping down as working royals in what was an acrimonious departure.
Harry's memoir, Spare, showed the depth of the family fall out and the damaged relationship with his brother William.
Despite Prince Harry now being physically nearer to his family in the UK, there hasn't seemed to be any more emotional closeness with his brother Prince William, and in this interview Harry seems to be open to reconciliation.
It was a message of wanting to build bridges that he had previously sent in a BBC interview in May 2025, when he had been living in the US.
Prince Harry recognised that this royal story of family disagreements fascinated the public, saying it was "massively relatable".
"Sibling disagreements, broken relationships between kids and their parents, kids and one parent - that continues to come up with me the whole time with people that I speak to," he said.
Asked by GQ about the reason for his move back to the UK, Prince Harry said: "Opportunities for the family. Being able to put the kids in a British school has meant a lot to me. I didn't know how important it was to me."
"They [Archie and Lilibet] are loving it, and it's just giving them a whole different experience."
He told the magazine: "To be back, closer to my family, and to be back on UK soil for longer than a few days or a week here or there".
Prince Harry also reflects on the King's health, following his treatment for cancer, saying: "He's getting better".
There were also comments about growing up with a sense of loss after the death of his mother, Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997.
"I love the fact that I'm able to now sort of carry the memory of my mother with me, with my work, rather than it hold me down, pull me back, or wallowing in that grief," he said.
He rejected any sense of wanting public sympathy.
"I certainly don't want any sympathy. That's where we're way past that. Why? Because I'm a prince. I've got a support network around me, I've done different forms of therapy, and I put in the work. I wonder where I would be if I didn't - it could be a very different situation," he said.

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment

From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.

A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
